paras: The killing of William Towey was the fatal shooting of a Black man by two sheriff's deputies near Huntsville, Alabama, on November 26, 1880. According to a Huntsville dispatch, Deputy-Sheriff Cooper and Special Deputy W. J. Franks shot Towey while trying to arrest him, after he raised a shotgun at them. The brief item ran in Chicago and Omaha papers under headlines that called him a "desperado" and a "Desperate Darky."

The officers held a writ of arrest for Towey, whom the dispatch called "a negro," and went to serve it near Huntsville; the charge on the writ is not stated. In the dispatch's words, Towey "raised a loaded shotgun and presented it at the officers, who immediately fired and killed him." The report added on hearsay ("it is said") that Towey "was a desperate character." This account is the only one in the coverage, it comes from the officers' side, and no version from Towey's family or other witnesses appears.
No report of an inquest, an inquiry into the deputies' conduct, or any later development was found.

The story reached the press as a single dispatch dated Huntsville, November 27, and appeared on November 29 in the Chicago Daily Tribune and the Omaha Daily Bee. The Tribune placed it among its criminal news under the heading "A NEGRO DESPERADO KILLED." The Bee printed nearly the same text as a special dispatch titled "Killed by Officers." and advertised it in its front-page deck as "A Desperate Darky Dies." Both papers repeated the officers' account as fact, and neither added comment of its own; no Alabama paper's report or Black-press coverage was found.

bases: Two named deputies shot and killed Towey while trying to serve a writ of arrest on him; no crowd or mob is mentioned (A1).
The only account is one Huntsville wire dispatch (A1), which ran with nearly identical text in the Omaha Bee (A2); no independent local or later report was found.

framing.detail: The Chicago Tribune headed the item 'A NEGRO DESPERADO KILLED' and repeated that Towey was 'a desperate character'; the shooting was presented as a response to his raising a shotgun.
The Omaha Bee ran the same dispatch as 'Killed by Officers.' under a front-page deck line 'A Desperate Darky Dies'.
